worker.about: The worker engine's value rows (run.py --engine worker; score.py --assert-worker). Each row's `worker` block lists its cases: `pre_cutover` must MATCH on every backend; `diverge` is a recorded divergence that must DIVERGE; `cutover` is run and shown but asserted only on the cutover candidate. Cases are compared by worker_compare.py: shared objects and sandbox ids up to relabelling, strings exactly. A case marked `local_refusal` expects the host to refuse its inputs before anything runs. A `diverge` case must differ in exactly the recorded fields and match the recorded worker value, so any other change fails. `cutover` cases must still run against an oracle.

divergences.name: unicode-normalization
divergences.what: CPython applies NFKC to a named tuple's field names when it builds the type; Dart has no Unicode normalization, so core's reader and writer accept two field names that normalize alike (K and KELVIN SIGN), where CPython 3.12 raises SyntaxError. No sandbox emits such a named tuple and upstream's host cannot build one as an input, so no case reaches it; core's fixtures cover it

divergences.name: unicode-version
divergences.what: core's validation and conversion use the platform's Unicode tables for Rust {:?} escaping in error messages, str.isidentifier() and repr() printability; measured against upstream over every code point, the only differences are characters that one side's Unicode version assigns and the other's does not (CPython 3.12 has Unicode 15.0). Reachable through a KeyError argument with an unpaired surrogate, which goes out as its repr (w_exc_unicode_version_in), and otherwise only through names and malformed arenas

divergences.name: timezone-refusal-wording
divergences.what: an unknown IANA zone name is refused at checkout by both: upstream raises ValueError "unknown timezone 'Not/AZone'" before any feed runs; core's session open raises ArgumentError "protocol violation: invalid os_policy: invalid value for SandboxTimeZone.named: unknown timezone 'Not/AZone'" (the worker's refusal of Configure). The case is a `local_refusal`, which matches on the refusal and ignores the type and wording, so the difference in type and message is recorded here, not asserted

w_exc_unicode_version_in.why: unicode-version: a KeyError argument with an unpaired surrogate goes out as its repr, and core's repr keeps U+1FAE9 (assigned in its Unicode tables) where CPython 3.12 (Unicode 15.0) escapes it as \U0001fae9

w_graph_cycle_ret.why: traceback-frames: a host callback returns a cyclic list. Upstream raises ValueError 'Circular reference detected' in the sandbox with no traceback frames; core raises the same type and message, with the call's frame `x = get()` in the traceback
